about:
# wow-addons

World of Warcraft: Forever addons by Odysseaus, built for the classic beta client (Interface `16001`). Each addon has its own folder, README, and GitHub Releases tag.

## Index

| Addon | Folder | Status | Get it |
|-------|--------|--------|--------|
| [WoW Grok](#wow-grok) | [`wow-grok/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok) | Released (Mac app, Windows app, addon zip) | [Releases](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases) (`wow-grok-mac-v…`, `wow-grok-win-v…`) |
| [WoW Threat](#wow-threat) | [`wow-threat/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-threat) | Released | [`wow-threat-v1.4.0`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-threat-v1.4.0) |
| [Dark Matter](#dark-matter) | [`dark-matter/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/dark-matter) | Released | [`dark-matter-v0.5.2b.9`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/dark-matter-v0.5.2b.9) |

## Where AddOns go

For any addon you install by copying a folder, put the folder in your AddOns directory:

- **Mac:** `/Applications/World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/`
- **Windows:** `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\`. Your drive letter or install folder may be different.

Then type `/reload` in game. If the game wasn't running, or the addon is brand new and doesn't show up, fully quit and relaunch WoW, then check that it's enabled under **AddOns** at character select.

---

## WoW Grok

Folder: [`wow-grok/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok) · In-game addon: [`wow-grok/addon/WoWGrok/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/addon/WoWGrok) · Full README: [`wow-grok/README.md`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/README.md)

Chat with your xAI Grok (API chat) from inside the game. Send a task, keep questing, and get pinged in game when the answer lands. Claude (Anthropic key) is an optional provider. A companion app on your Mac or Windows PC sends your message to the API with **your** key. Addons can't go online, so the app reads a strip of colored pixels the addon draws on screen and writes replies back into AddOn files the game loads.

- Open it with `/wow-grok` or `/grok` (also `/ai`, `/ask`).
- Shift-click items, spells, and quests into the input to insert links.
- Multiple chats, a status light, and reply recovery.
- The addon list shows version `0.1.22` (Author: chelinho139). It's based on the MIT [wow-claude](https://github.com/chelinho139/wow-claude), with the companion bridge rewritten in Python.
- **Not supported:** GeForce Now, Shadow, or any cloud or streaming WoW. The app must run on the same computer as a normal local WoW install.

  ![WoW Grok chat window in game, answering a question about dungeons at level 20](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/main/wow-grok/docs/screenshot.png)

*The WoW Grok chat window in game.*

  ![The upstream wow-claude chat window in Elwynn Forest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/main/wow-grok/docs/screenshot.jpg)

*The same chat window in upstream wow-claude (this image comes from that project).*

### Download & install

WoW Grok installs differently from the other addons. **Don't copy the folder by hand.** Download the companion app. It finds your AddOns folder (or asks you for it), writes the `WoWGrok` addon plus its reply slots (`WoWGrok_S001`–`WoWGrok_S200`), and then keeps running as the bridge while you play. You need an API key from [console.x.ai](https://console.x.ai/) (the default), or a Claude key. Mac and Windows are separate downloads.

**Mac** ([step by step](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/docs/INSTALL-MAC.md))

1. From [Releases](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases), get the newest `wow-grok-mac-v…` build: `WoWGrok.dmg` or `WoWGrok-mac-arm64.zip`. Right now [`wow-grok-mac-v0.1.31`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-grok-mac-v0.1.31) is marked pre-release and [`wow-grok-mac-v0.1.30`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-grok-mac-v0.1.30) is the newest full release. Both are Apple Silicon (arm64) builds.
2. Drag **WoWGrok.app** into Applications and launch it from there. The build is unsigned, so **Control-click → Open**, then **Open Anyway** in Privacy & Security if macOS asks.
3. In the setup wizard, pick Grok (xAI) or Claude, paste your key, and confirm your `Interface/AddOns` folder. Grant **Screen Recording**, and quit and reopen once if it asks. Leave the **menu bar** icon running.

**Windows** ([step by step](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/docs/INSTALL-WINDOWS.md))

1. Download `WoWGrok.exe` from the newest `wow-grok-win-v…` release. Right now that's [`wow-grok-win-v0.1.31`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-grok-win-v0.1.31).
2. Run it. The build is unsigned, so if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info → Run anyway**.
3. In the setup wizard, pick xAI or Claude, paste your key, and confirm your `Interface\AddOns` folder. Leave the **tray** icon **Running**.

**Then, on both:** play in **Windowed** or **Windowed (Fullscreen)** mode. Exclusive fullscreen blocks the screen read. **Fully quit and relaunch** WoW, because `/reload` doesn't pick up brand-new AddOns. At character select, enable **WoW Grok** and leave the `WoW Grok slot ###` entries on. Type `/wow-grok` or `/grok`.

There's also an addon-only zip, [`wow-grok-addon-v0.1.22`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-grok-addon-v0.1.22) (`WoWGrok-0.1.22.zip`). It holds just the in-game `WoWGrok` folder: no app and no reply slots. The addon can't get replies without the companion app running, so most players should use the app above.

More: [all-platform overview](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/docs/INSTALL-USERS.md) · [how it works](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [configuration](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) · [changelog](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-grok/CHANGELOG.md)

## WoW Threat

Folder: [`wow-threat/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-threat) · Addon: [`wow-threat/WoWThreat/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/wow-threat/WoWThreat)

A single, clean threat meter for Forever. It lists your group against your hostile target with the highest threat on top, using the client's `UnitDetailedThreatSituation`.

- **One bar meter:** each row shows the first name (realm stripped, long names cut off with …, class-colored text) above a black bar, with % and raw threat (12.3k) on the right. Your own row gets a theme-colored outline and stays pinned when you fall outside the shown rows.
- **The fire is the bar:** the default "Fireplace" fire is a baked, seamless flame wall whose width is your threat %. It's cropped, never stretched, and its tips rise above the bar. It has sparks, a glow and a white-hot core above 90%. A lighter "Classic" style, "Castbar fire" (layered scrolling fire, smoke and embers, new in 1.2.0) and "Off" (plain bar) are also available. All fire art is original and generated by `wow-threat/tools/`.
- **WoW theme (default since 1.4.0):** a stock-looking frame drawn with the game's own textures, referenced in game by path and never bundled: the tooltip border and background, the dialog title plate with a GameFontNormal gold title, and the stock status bar (`TargetingFrame\UI-StatusBar`) as the bar track and plain fill. Each texture is checked at runtime; any the client lacks falls back to WoWThreat's own look. `/wtm artprobe` lists which were found (ok / MISSING) and saves the list to `WoWThreatDB.artprobe`. A saved Auto theme moves to WoW once on upgrade; choosing Auto again afterwards sticks.
- **Five themes:** Ember Hall (Auto for other classes), Ironforged (Warrior), Ursine Grove (Druid), Dawnward (Paladin) and Voidbound (Warlock). Each has a textured frame, corners, crest, medallion and plaque, a light animation (gem glow, rocking swords plus a glint, rustling leaves, a turning sun with motes and a light sweep, pulsing runes with wisps). Every theme uses the same Ironforged fire. Auto picks by class.
- **Motion:** bars and numbers count smoothly, rows slide to their new rank, and a new #1 gets a short pop.
- **Columns:** Auto or 1–4, ranked across columns and capped at about 60% of the screen width, with up to 10 rows per column. Rows fade out when combat ends. With more than 20 rows the fire drops its glow layer and sparks stay on the top 10.
- **Edit Mode:** open Edit Mode to see a blue "WoW Threat" selection with preview rows. Drag it (snaps to 8 px), or click it for Scale, Max rows, Bar width, Columns, Theme, Fire style and Reset position. Positions are saved per Edit Mode layout. The meter can't be moved outside Edit Mode.
- **Options panel:** Esc > Options > AddOns > WoW Threat (or `/wtm options`): Max rows, Columns, Bar width, Row height, Scale, Theme, Animate frame, Show fire, Fire style, Fire intensity, Fire speed, Flame overflow, Fire sound (off by default; SFX channel, in combat only), Reduced effects, Show pop, Number format, Show only in group, Hide out of combat, Class colors, Test mode and Reset position. It stays in sync with the Edit Mode dialog.
- **Slash commands** (`/wtm` or `/wowthreat`): `options`, `test [raid20|raid40|swap|swapfast]`, `theme <wow|auto|emberhall|ironforged|ursinegrove|dawnward|voidbound>`, `style <fireplace|classic|castbar|gem|off>`, `fire <0-1|off|on>`, `reset`, `debug` (prints one threat-scale line per unit), `probe` (API check), `artprobe` (stock textures for the WoW theme). Anything else prints the help.
- Settings are saved in `WoWThreatDB` (schema v3). Upgrades from 0.1.x and 1.0.0 migrate automatically.
- Version `1.4.0`, released as [`wow-threat-v1.4.0`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-threat-v1.4.0), Interface `16001`.

### Download & install

1. Download the `WoWThreat` zip from the latest `wow-threat-v…` release on the [releases page](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases). The latest is [`wow-threat-v1.4.0`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/wow-threat-v1.4.0) (`WoWThreat-1.4.0.zip`).
2. Unzip it. You'll get a `WoWThreat` folder, which includes `Textures/`.
3. Copy the `WoWThreat` folder into your AddOns directory, replacing any older copy:
   - Mac: `/Applications/World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/`
   - Windows: `C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\` (your drive or install folder may differ)
4. Type `/reload` in game, then `/wtm test` to see it, or open Edit Mode to place it.

## Dark Matter

Folder: [`dark-matter/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/dark-matter) · Addon: [`dark-matter/DarkMatter/`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/dark-matter/DarkMatter) · Full README: [`dark-matter/README.md`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/dark-matter/README.md) · [Changelog](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/blob/main/dark-matter/CHANGELOG.md)

One window for your quests, map, journals and dungeons in WoW Forever, drawn in the game's own window art by default.

- **Map tab:** the game's world map from Azeroth down to each zone, with numbered zoom levels, painted zone maps blended across borders, zone level ranges, close-up minimap tiles at the deepest zoom, place names, quest areas and POI buttons. Full screen zooms the same way as the window.
- **Quests:** your quest log with zone headers, search and quest detail; quest pins with game icons on the map; a docked quest log beside the map; and a Ready to Turn In list below the tracker.
- **Journals:** Fishing (waters, catches, a full catch catalog with item tooltips, and statistics), Adventure Guide and Achievements.
- **Themes:** the default WoW theme uses the stock window art; class themes are options. Open it with `/dm` or the minimap button.
- **Classic Era test bench:** `DarkMatter_Vanilla.toc` loads the same code on Classic Era for testing; Forever loads `DarkMatter.toc`.

### Screenshots

> In-game captures from test builds on Oct 23, 2026 (0.5.2b.8 and 0.5.2b.8.1), cropped to the window. Test captions and seams between zone pictures were reduced in later builds.

  ![Dark Matter Map tab showing Eastern Kingdoms at zoom 4 with zone level ranges, beside the docked quest log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/main/dark-matter/docs/dm-map-continent.jpg)

*Eastern Kingdoms with zone level ranges, and the docked quest log on the right.*

  ![Dark Matter Map tab zoomed into Deadwind Pass and its neighbours, with level ranges per zone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/main/dark-matter/docs/dm-map-zone-levels.jpg)

*Zoomed in around Deadwind Pass: painted zone maps with their level ranges.*

  ![Dark Matter Map tab at a deep zoom over Swamp of Sorrows showing detailed terrain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/main/dark-matter/docs/dm-map-closeup.jpg)

*A close-up of Swamp of Sorrows.*

### Download & install

1. Download `DarkMatter-0.5.2b.9.zip` from [`dark-matter-v0.5.2b.9`](https://github.com/Odysseaus/wow-addons/releases/tag/dark-matter-v0.5.2b.9).
2. Unzip it. You'll get a `DarkMatter` folder.
3. Copy the `DarkMatter` folder into your AddOns directory (see [Where AddOns go](#where-addons-go)), replacing any older copy.
4. Type `/reload` in game (or relaunch WoW if it's a first install), then `/dm` to open it.

releases.name: Valhalla 1.2.59
releases.notes:
Valhalla 1.2.59 for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). This release also includes 1.2.56 through 1.2.58.

- **Quest log pin on the left (1.2.59).** In the quest log, Valhalla's pin is back on the left of each quest's icon, as before 1.2.51 and as in the Objectives panel.
- **Shared Auction House scans (1.2.58).** Top 10, Scan Results and History are shared by every character: one market each for the Alliance, Horde and Neutral houses. Watchlist targets stay this character's. Scans that had been saved under different names for the same realm are brought together once, so an alt sees the same prices without scanning again.
- **The game's quest icons, Valhalla's click (1.2.57).** Quest icons on the zone you're looking at are the game's own again, one per quest (its tooltip with the quest's level), with no Valhalla copy on top. Clicking one does what Valhalla's quest icons do: it selects the quest, showing its area and the minimap waypoint, and a second click clears it. It never tracks or untracks a quest. Shift-click adds the quest's link only when the chat is already open. Quests in the neighbouring zones keep Valhalla's icons.
- **Quest icons current on open (1.2.56).** Quest icons on the map are up to date the moment you open it: a quest completed (or changed) while the map was closed shows at its new place at once, instead of its old place for half a second first.

**Install:** unzip and copy the `Valhalla` folder into `Interface/AddOns/`. From 1.2.44 or later, a /reload is enough. From 1.2.43 or earlier, fully restart the game, because new files were added.

releases.name: Valhalla 1.2.55
releases.notes:
Valhalla 1.2.55 for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). This release also includes 1.2.39 through 1.2.54.

- **Shift-click never changes the Objectives panel (1.2.53–1.2.55).** With the chat closed, Shift-clicking a quest's title or icon in the quest log, or a quest's header or icon in the Objectives panel, no longer tracks or untracks it: the panel stays as it was, and a selection the click changed is put back. Shift-click no longer opens the chat line. With the chat line already open, Shift-click puts the quest's link in it as the game does, including on a quest's pin, and a Shift-click never pins or unpins.
- **The Objectives panel follows the zone (1.2.52).** It lists only this zone's quests (as the quest log files them) and your pinned ones; another zone's quest no longer joins because its objective area reaches here. Ready to Turn In still lists a ready quest you can hand in here.
- **Townsfolk: one icon per NPC (1.2.51).** Lakeshire, Bloodhoof Village and the cities no longer show pairs on the world map or minimap, and Lakeshire's icons sit where the NPCs stand. The quest log's quest icons stay where the game puts them; Valhalla's pin sits just right of the icon.
- **Quest clicks and selection (1.2.48–1.2.50).**
  - Clicking a quest icon on the map shows the quest's area and its minimap waypoint; a second click clears it. Selecting or deselecting a quest never adds quests to the Objectives panel or takes them off.
  - Selecting a quest on the map opens its zone in the quest log and scrolls to it.
  - Clicking a quest's icon in the quest log keeps it selected and flies the map to it, without flashing it into the Objectives panel.
  - Pinned quests' pins glow in the quest log and the Objectives panel; unpinned pins are dimmer.
- **Townsfolk icon size (1.2.47).** In the menu's Townsfolk section: Large, Medium or Small on the world map, for each character.
- **Quest icons and the minimap (1.2.43–1.2.46).**
  - Quest icons on the map are the quest log's own buttons, at the log's size on every zone.
  - Townsfolk on the minimap stay on their spot as you walk. Inns, banks, mailboxes, auctioneers, stable masters, repair, food, reagents and class trainers on the minimap come from the game's own tracking, never twice.
  - Profession icons use their own pictures, with a checkbox to turn them on and off.
- **Map settings follow the character (1.2.42).** Townsfolk, professions, the minimap, flight masters and the other map switches are saved for each character, starting as the account had them.
- **Townsfolk (1.2.39–1.2.41).** Inns, repair, mailboxes, banks, auctioneers, stables, spirit healers, vendors, and class and profession trainers from Wowhead WoW Forever, each type with its own checkbox and one Townsfolk switch for all. Each profession has its own checkbox (trainers and suppliers together); every class's trainers are on the map, the other faction's hidden. The same pins show on the minimap. No other addon is required.

**Install:** unzip and copy the `Valhalla` folder into `Interface/AddOns/`. From 1.2.44 or later, a /reload is enough. From 1.2.43 or earlier (including 1.2.38), fully restart the game, because new files were added.

releases.name: Valhalla 1.2.38
releases.notes:
Valhalla 1.2.38 for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). This release also includes 1.2.32 through 1.2.37 (there was no 1.2.33 release).

- **Quest log rows no longer overlap when you turn Ready on or off (1.2.38).** Turning Show Ready to Turn In on or off lays the quest log out again, so a quest row isn't left on top of another row or a zone header. The zones stay alphabetical.
- **Quest chains rebuilt from Wowhead WoW Forever (1.2.37).**
  - Built from Wowhead's Series boxes only: 755 chains, 2,618 quests. A quest whose page has no Series box still gets no chain button.
  - `/valhalla chain coverage` lists your quest log's quests and their chain status, and saves the last 3 runs with your character.
- **No more Lua error after leveling up (1.2.35, 1.2.36).**
  - For about 2 seconds after you level, Valhalla waits before it changes tracked quests, the quest you follow or the quest log's order.
  - The quest log's order is kept only while the log is open, and laid out again only when it actually changed.
- **Flight masters and the map's settings (1.2.34).**
  - No flight masters at Eastern Plaguelands' towers, where no character can learn them. Mount Hyjal's two, Summit of Eternity and Tainted Foothills, are on the map with their routes.
  - The map can no longer go blank from a view worked out while it was 0 pixels wide. A saved window place, size or scale that isn't a real number is forgotten, so one bad number can't make the game reset every setting.
- **Craft: Cost/item (1.2.32).** The Cost to Make column is now Cost/item: what one item costs, the craft's reagents divided by how many one craft makes, so every row adds up. A craft that makes more than one shows "x2" (or "x1-3") after its name, and its tooltip adds Cost per item.

**Install:** unzip and copy the `Valhalla` folder into `Interface/AddOns/`. From 1.2.26 or later, a /reload is enough. From 1.2.25 or earlier, fully restart the game, because 1.2.26 added new files.

SHA-256 of Valhalla-1.2.38.zip: `e924fed3a3ff0c8cdbedf37a2245317582ce89e7c63694028687e89384152fc7`

releases.name: Valhalla 1.2.31
releases.notes:
Valhalla 1.2.31 for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). This release also includes 1.2.24 through 1.2.30.

- **Dungeon Journal's dungeon map no longer covers the other tabs (1.2.31).** Inside a dungeon, the Dungeon Journal add-on's map (with its World Map and Scarlet Monastery wing buttons) stayed over Investments, Talents, Professions and Settings. It's now put away when you leave Map & Quest Log. When you come back, it's just as you left it: the same wing and floor, or its World Map if you'd picked that.
- **Your Watchlist, AH history, Top 10 and lists are back (1.2.29, 1.2.30).** After WoW Forever's 1.60.1.71037 update, the game names your realm differently at login, so your saved Investments data looked gone. Nothing was deleted.
  - Valhalla now waits for the realm name and never saves under a blank one.
  - A character with saved data keeps its saved realm, whatever the game calls it. Characters on different realms are never mixed.
  - On the first load, anything saved under the wrong name is merged back once: scans in time order, the newer bag and bank counts, and lists added without duplicates.
  - `/valhalla invest realm` shows which realm Valhalla uses and why.
- **Craft's search (1.2.27, 1.2.28).**
  - Two tick boxes: Item Name (the default) or All. All also finds the words you type in a craft's reagents, so "thread" lists every craft that uses a thread. Your choice is kept.
  - Fishing's Harvest list now has eels, clams and the other catches the game files as Other.
- **Fixes from a full code review (1.2.26).**
  - The quest log waits for combat to end before Valhalla lays it out.
  - Pin codes with spaces in their notes share in full.
  - Deleting a pin closes its note.
  - What's new scrolls.
  - Investments: fixes to mail, item loading and tooltips.
- **Waypoints and zone tracking (1.2.24, 1.2.25).** Quest tracker changes wait for combat and secret auras against the "secret while tainted by 'Valhalla'" error. Out of combat they apply at once again. `/valhalla combat` shows what's waiting.

**Install:** unzip and copy the `Valhalla` folder into `Interface/AddOns/`. From 1.2.26 or later, a /reload is enough. From 1.2.25 or earlier, fully restart the game, because 1.2.26 added new files.

releases.name: Valhalla 1.2.23
releases.notes:
Valhalla 1.2.23 for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). This release also includes 1.2.21 and 1.2.22.

- **No more "Auras cannot be accessed when secret while tainted by 'Valhalla'" in combat (1.2.23):** a spec or talent change in combat lays out the game's quest tracker again, and it reads your auras. That read errored when Valhalla's own changes to the tracker had come just before.
  - In combat, Valhalla now leaves the quest tracker and quest log alone and makes its changes once combat ends.
  - Tracking a quest in combat (a Ready to Turn In row, a quest's icon on the map, or Shift-click on a quest chain row) applies when combat ends, with one line in chat.
  - In combat, Valhalla's menu, Pins, the Quill and its settings button open the map once combat ends. The map's own keys and buttons work as before.
  - While the quest log is open beside the map, the map no longer switches to the zone you're looking at. Close the quest log and it follows the view again.
- **Quest log zones stay as you leave them (1.2.22):** a zone you click open or folded stays that way for each character, after map changes, loading screens, a /reload and a log-in. Zones you've never clicked still follow the game.
- **The druids' flight from Nighthaven is timed (1.2.21):** Silva Fil'naveth's flight to Rut'theran Village (and Bunthen Plainswind's to Thunder Bluff) now shows the destination, is timed and saved, and counts down next time. Nighthaven counts as a learned flight master once you've flown from it.

**Install:** unzip and copy the `Valhalla` folder into `Interface/AddOns/`. From 1.2.19 or later, a /reload is enough. From 1.2.17 or earlier, fully restart the game, because 1.2.18 added map textures.
